races.title: State House, District 20
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Tim Merrick
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for North Carolina House District 20. A chiropractic physician (New York Chiropractic College, 1991) and small-business owner for more than 45 years, according to his campaign. Ballotpedia lists him as a member of the New Hanover County Board of Education.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Tim Merrick was born or raised, or when he moved to North Carolina. We found no dates for his school board service and no record of his votes or actions on that board. We found no stated position on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns or abortion. His stance on school vouchers and charters is also unknown; he says he supports fully funded public schools. We found no notable endorsements, only listings in informal voter-guide groups.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Chiropractic physician and small-business owner for more than 45 years who has met payroll. He serves on the New Hanover County Board of Education, an elected local office, per Ballotpedia. He has no listed experience in the state legislature.
qual.why: The score falls in the middle band for local elected office plus business ownership and management. There is no prior legislative service or budget or policy career to move it higher.
qual.label: The score falls in the middle band for local elected office plus business ownership and management. There is no prior legislative service or budget or policy career to move it higher.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: His campaign site says he wants balanced, responsible growth that protects neighborhoods and the environment, not unchecked expansion, and calls him a defender of clean water and responsible development.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 1 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised (needs 2 to score)

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Campaign site: "We deserve development that protects our neighborhoods, our environment, and our quality of life—not unchecked expansion that benefits only a few."

cands.name: Dane Scalise
cands.bio: Republican candidate for North Carolina House District 20 in the November 3, 2026 general election against Democrat Tim Merrick. His campaign site describes him as a New Hanover County Commissioner. His Republican primary was canceled and he advanced without appearing on the ballot.
cands.gaps: We found no independently verified record of Scalise's actions as a county commissioner, such as county board votes, budgets or meeting minutes. His claims of cutting taxes, voting for green space, record school and law enforcement funding, and ending a county program come only from his campaign site. We could not find his birthplace, where he grew up or when he came to North Carolina. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, foreign or institutional land buying, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, and Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him. We found no controversies or foreign ties in the pages reviewed.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: His campaign site says he is a New Hanover County Commissioner. No other career or legislative history appears in the pages reviewed.
qual.why: Local elected office puts him in the middle band. No prior legislative service or law, policy or budget career was found, so he scores below the high band.
qual.label: Local elected office puts him in the middle band. No prior legislative service or law, policy or budget career was found, so he scores below the high band.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: His campaign site pledges to hold government to spending within its means and to reevaluate the tax code to give relief to families and seniors on fixed incomes. It says he fought to keep taxes low as a commissioner despite property revaluations. This is his own description, not an independently verified record.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: His campaign site says he opposed developments that would damage local neighborhoods and repeatedly voted for green space and parks over new developments. It also says he supports long-term economic growth and protecting green spaces. These are his own claims, not checked against meeting records.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he delivered record funding to law enforcement and ended a county-funded violence-prevention program that employed active gang members. These are his own claims, not checked against county records.

prio.label: Matches 3 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 3 only promised
